text: Abon Duum was a human man and a pasha of Manshaka in Calimshan in the 14th century DR.
Aban al-Hadhar was a gnome barber who lived in Hawa in 1367 DR.
Aasim al-Gammam was a tasked administrator genie who was in charge of the South Center of Huzuz in 1367 DR.
Aasim was an elven sha'ir living on Masud Jazayir in the Crowded Sea in 1367 DR.
Abu Jafar was a bandit and member of the Desert Wind during the mid–14th century DR.
Achreny Ulyeltin was a merchant just before the Tyranny of Dragons.
Emir Abi Talid was the ruler of Iliphanar in Semphar during the later 14th century DR.
Abul Fiydah was the Amir of Estanil during the mid–14th century DR.
Aasim al-Nazi was a priest of the Golden Mosque in Huzuz, the City of Delights, in 1367 DR.

Lady Aalangama Gulderhorn was Countess of Morninggold, Title Chancellor of Tethyr, Marquise Scion of Siamorphe, and commander and one of the founders of the Order of the Silver Chalice. She was also the unofficial Crown Ecclesiastic of Tethyr.
Achmed al-Assad was the father of Khalil al-Assad al-Zahir—the Grand Caliph of Huzuz in 1367 DR.
Abu bin Sujah was a renowned Zakharan desert rider who sought the fabled city of Suj around 1367 DR.
Abadda Moonglamaer was a prince of Phalorm, the Realm of Three Crowns.
Achtel Gnarlfingers was a shaman of Gruumsh who represented the largest tribe in attendance during the destruction of Shallows.
Able was a warrior-cleric of Tyr who was a part of the rescue team sent to the Utter East to rescue Piergeiron the Paladinson's bride circa 1371 DR.
Aasim Karim was a Zakharan desert rider and head of the House of Al-Karim living in the desert outside of Hiyal around 1367 DR.

Lord Abarel Stendale was the general of the military forces of Melvaunt around 1367 DR. Abarel's title of Lord was simply an honorific title; he was not a member of the Council of Lords. By 1373, he had lost his position and was only a mercenary captain.

Abeils (sometimes pluralized as "abeil"), also commonly known as bee people, were humanoid bee-like creatures that lived in large hive-cities. They were divided into three castes: the laboring vassals, the fighting soldiers (also known as stormwings), and the ruling queens.
Aberdeen Krestner was one of the three guildmasters of the Diviner's Guild in Ravens Bluff in the 14 century DR.
Achen Dell was a mercenary who lived in the Realms during the mid–14 century DR.
Abbey Fargo was a soldier in the Neverwinter Guard who served during the late 15 century DR.
Achiko was the son of a noble of Aru Province in Wa in the 1700s on the Wa Calendar.
Abelar Corrinthal was a holy warrior of Lathander of Sembia in the late 14 century DR. Though he later fell from grace, in the end he regained his faith.
Abyssal wretches were a type of fiend created by mutating a humanoid.
A'lai Aivenmore was one of the eight Great Readers of the Avowed that served Candlekeep during the late 15 century DR.
Caliph Abir al-Farhan, also called the Humble Servant of the Enlightened Gods, was the ruler of Hilm in the Pantheist League of interior Zakhara in 1367 DR.
Abu Karesan was a guard for the slaver ring in the Oasis of the White Palm.
High Lord Abalazmer Harauntan was the ruler of Yhep along the Lake of Steam during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
A. Grekov was a Raumviran innkeeper who lived in Almorel on the Lake of Mists in the Hordelands in the .

Abu Bahar was a salesman in the town of Bralizzar who specialized in harnesses. They were known to be active in the mid-14 century DR. Their shop was the second from the north, a small one on the eastern side of the city's bazaar.
Absolute was a traveling bard and entertainer from the Dragon Reach in the The Vast, active in the late 14 century DR.
Achem el Zalath was a Calishite wizard of Almraiven in eastern Calimshan during the late 14 century DR.
Abrix Myll was a Zhentish merchant and agent who worked in Thentia in 1367 DR.
Acciajuoli was a Netherese arcanist and co-owner of Transgate Industries, who lived in Karsus Enclave until its destruction in .
Abyssal Gavin was a female drow inhabitant of the city of Baldur's Gate in late 15 century DR.
Aawlynson was one of the bandits under the Iron Fox in the mid–8 century DR.
Abella Toth was one of the Magistrates of Cormyr, who worked in Eveningstar and Wheloon in the late 15 century DR.
Abaforth Zelksix was a duergar from the Lower City of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.

Achmed yn Nuram el Darkiir yi Almraiven was a human thief and mage from Almraiven, Calimshan, and the secret leader of the Many Long Arms, the private thieves' guild and spy network of the Rundeen mercantile organization in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Aencar Burlisk () was a Dalesfolk hero who united all of the Dalelands (with the exception of Archendale and High Dale), in the early-to-mid-11 century DR.

Adon was a devout cleric of Sune that served the goddess Mystra later in life. He was a prominent personality of the Time of Troubles that broke out during the mid–14 century DR and played an important role in the apotheosis of Midnight as the new goddess of magic.
Ad'non Kareese was a male drow and a member of a band of four renegades including Donnia Soldou, Kaer'lic Suun Wett, and Tos'un Armgo.
Agrathan Hardhammer was a dwarf cleric of Dumathoin and a member of the Council of Sparkling Stones of Mirabar in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Prince Aglarel Tanthul was one of the twelve original Princes of Shade, the sons of Telamont Tanthul that came to Faerûn on the eve of the Return in the late 14 century DR.
Aguul was a ogre printer who lived in the city of Procampur in the Vast in the mid–14 century DR.
Adalwulf Longfang was the honorable chieftain of the Uthgardt Red Tiger tribe located primarily in the Cold Wood.
Aganis was a human man from the village of Pengallen in the Silver Marches. He was a barkeep of the local inn.

Agathinon (singular and plural, ; also singular agathion, , and plural agathia) were good-natured spiritual messengers and warriors from the Upper Planes. The Netherese goddess of magic, Mystryl, employed these angels as messengers, along with many other noble beings.

Afafrenfere was a human monk of the Brothers of the Gray Mists and a former member of the Bounty Hunters of Cavus Dun. He was saved from death by fellow Cavus Dun member Ambergris; the two then traveled with Drizzt Do'Urden and his companions until Drizzt's apparent demise at Kelvin's Cairn. At the splintering of the group, Afafrenfere sought penance at the Monastery of the Yellow Rose, with Ambergris as his companion, before he was assigned to journey with the drow Jarlaxle.
Adolican Rhand was a Waterdeep noble wizard who worked for the Shadovar.

Adhan el Ilmater was a human man and a priest of Ilmater. He was the leader of the House of the Broken God temple in Keltar, Calimshan, circa 1370 DR. Adhan was a kind and wise man, who often worked directly with his patients. He was gray-haired and balding, but usually smiling.
Adanac Harpell was the elder of the Harpell family and spokesman for the town of Longsaddle in the Savage Frontier in the 14 century DR.

Adimond Kroskas was the leader of a Cult of the Dragon cell in Neverwinter circa 1480 DR. He was enslaved by Valindra Shadowmantle, who also gained his ring of dragons. However, he agreed to her project of resurrecting the legendary dragon Lorragauth as a dracolich. However, the problems stalling the project put him under a lot of stress, being caught between the elven lich and his Cult subordinates.
Addemios Three-Dawn was an high elf priest and secret devotee of Asmodeus who masqueraded as a follower Corellon at the Temple of Leaves in New Sharandar.
Afrafa was a female human monk and a member of the Disciples of St. Sollars the Twice-Martyred at the Monastery of the Yellow Rose in the mid–14th century DR.
Adun Abd al-Amin was the general and commander of the Faithful Mamluk Society in Qudra in 1367 DR.
Adama Miiralin was a young and naive cleric of Tymora in Waterdeep in 1372 DR.
Ackyn Selebon was a merchant of Baldur's Gate during the Tyranny of Dragons.
Ser Agin Lamarck was a nobleman and historian at Mantor's Library in Phlan during the late 15 century DR.
Adrienne Stillwater was a female half-elf ranger and cleric of Mielikki operating in the Hullack Forest and the town of Thunderstone in Cormyr in the late 1360s DR.
Adisha Brombottle was a halfling merchant at the Monastery of the Yellow Rose in the late 15 century DR.
Aekyl Dafyre was a shopkeeper in Skullport during the late 14 century DR.

Aglast Thimm was a wizard and a member of the Zhentarim. He served as a mageling to Ruatheene and was based in a Zhentilar camp in the valley of Arntethyl by the river Tesh. Previously, Aglast acted as a poisoner for the Zhents in various Sea of Fallen Stars cities until his face became too known.

Adan Longstride was an ambassador to the goblin realm of the Kingdom of Nix in the Utter East during the time of the Bloodforge Wars (648–657 DR). In the midst of council, Adan Longstride maligned the good will of the leader of the Legendary Campaign, who had been appointed emissary to Nix with the task of negotiating peace terms with the king of the goblins. In accordance with goblin custom, they had to resolve their disagreement in trial by combat, which they did through bloodforge battle.
Aelric the Avenger was a warrior-mage who tried to liberate the kingdom of Doegan in the Utter East during the time of the Bloodforge Wars (648–657 DR).
Adras Ashatiel was the heir of the Ashatiel noble family of Waterdeep circa the mid–14 century DR. She later served as the right hand to Caelar Argent within the Shining Crusade army.
Aerel Hassammar was the owner and operator of the Swords Meet inn and tavern located in Voonlar, circa the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR.

Adresin was a knight of the Golden Star who had joined Seiveril Miritar's crusade. In 1374 DR, during the Cormanthor War, he acted as Seiveril's herald and adjutant on the field of battle. Later, he died fighting alone at the Semberholme border.
Goodwoman Aelia was a healer and herbalist in the Moonsea in the late 15 century DR.
Lord Agrak () was a cambion goblin lord and chief servant of Graz'zt in the Moonsea in the late 15 century DR.
Agaricus was one of the myconid rulers in Sporedome in the late 15 century DR.
Aglatha Shrey was a half-ogre order clerk for the Aurora's Realms Shop, Slut Street Catalogue Counter in the Dock Ward of Waterdeep in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Aevan Dragorovich was a Raumviran inhabitant of Drubiev in the Hordelands in 1375 DR.
Agrorn Silverleaf was an elven ranger who unsuccessfully searched for the power of spellfire.

Aedelthrang the Black was a cleric of Uthgar in the Red Tiger tribe of Uthgardt barbarians that lived in the Silver Marches during the mid-14 century DR. He was an important authority figure within the tribe, serving as their "spirit talker". Although the tribe was officially led by Chieftain Thradulf Longfang, following the death of his uncle Adalwulf, Adelthrang acted as their true leader.
Aglanthol the Red was the second High Mage of Silverymoon, having taking over as leader of the city from his uncle, Ecamane Truesilver in 712 DR.

Aghebar was an agent of the Zhentarim during the mid-to-late 14 century DR. He was a subordinate of the Head of Caravans Meer, both before and after the rise of Fzoul Chembryl within the Black Network. Aghebar had a number of low-level Zhentarim merchants who reported directly to him.
Agorn Fuoco () was a high-ranking member of Manshoon's Zhentarim in Waterdeep during the early 1490s DR.

Adarus were cunning, mobile tanar'ri demons with a love for collecting, whether it was treasure, minions, or unique body parts. The venomous fiends were beings of utter corruption, vile treachery and poisonous lies given form.
Ahbaer Milshoun was a failed Calishite merchant who owned Milshoun's Stronghouses in the village of Beliard around the .
Lieutenant Aegisfield was an inspector who served the Athkatlan Magistrate during the mid–14 century DR.
Aerix Vokototh () was a young Reghedmen of the Tribe of the Wolf who lived in Icewind Dale during the late 15 century DR.
Aelgar the Fierce was a barbarian who took up residence in the city of Neverwinter for a time during the late 15 century DR.
Adabra Gwynn was an acolyte of Chauntea who lived in a stone windmill on Umbrage Hill in the late 15 century DR.
Adjam el Drakhon was syl-pasha of Calimport during the Third age of Calimshan.
Lucky Aello was a rather unscrupulous shopkeeper and the proprietor of Lucky Aello's Discount Store in Baldur's Gate during the mid–14 century DR.
Agat amir-Doth was a middle-aged elf and the Chief Vizier of Jumlat in the Pearl Cities region of west Zakhara in 1367 DR.
Afzal was a prince of Tajar in the Pearl Cities of Zakhara in 1367 DR and the bane of his father's existence.
Adil al-Jazarijja was a member of the House of Hanif tribe within the Haunted Lands in 1367 DR.
Aeraldoth was a djinn vizier of the Grand Caliph. He volunteered to be imprisoned by Martek in order to do battle with Khalitharius upon his release.
Caliph Agara al-Gandar, who was also called Agara the Dandy was the ruler of the Free City of Utaqa in north Zakhara in .

Aeryll was a ranger of the Yuirwood in the mid-to-late 14 century DR. He was barely a year out of his Jalesh Rudra, hardly more than a boy according to Chereth, when he participated in torturing Kheil on the night of Mirtul 2, .
Aelar was a druid of the Emerald Grove circa the late 15 century DR.
Adyan Mercatio was the scion of the noble House Mercatio of Arrabar in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Aetheric III was the emperor of Doegan in the Utter East in the late 14 century.
Aeroth was a leader of the Cult of the Dragon based out of Karthaut Lighthouse, and the Wearer of Purple for his cell during the late 14 century DR.
Aelbronter Dauntrael was a member of the Dauntrael clan as of .
Adyat al Hayat was a salesman in the town of Bralizzar who specialized in cloth. They were known to be active in the mid-14 century DR. Their shop was the largest one on the east side of the bazaar.
Lord Adorellan was an inhabitant of Cormanthor in the 3 century DR.
Lady Aelieyeeva was an inhabitant of Cormanthor in the 3 century DR.
Aerendyl Tassarion was an inhabitant of Cormanthyr in the 3 century DR.
Aeorian hunters were monstrous entities created by the Red Wizards of Thay, by means of magical experiments involving humanoid races and monsters.
Agamur was a pit fiend in the late 14 century DR slain by the Simbul.
Aelrue was a moon elf neighbor of Elminster Aumar in the mid-14 century DR.
Aerlyse was a half-drow psion and a member of Bregan D'aerthe as of the late 15 century DR.
The dwarf Adhamh () was a gravedigger in Waterdeep during the late 15 century DR.
Adrey Foxrun was a young girl who lived in at Fourstaves House in Yhaunn in 1373 DR.
King Adbar was a historical dwarven ruler of Citadel Adbar in Luruar during the waning years of Delzoun.
Aeroth of Silverymoon was a War Captain and champion of Silverymoon during the Second Trollwar in the 10 century DR. Later in life, he relocated his family to the Moonshae Isles.
Pip was the butler at the Balthis Estate in the City of Coin, Athkatla in the late 14 century DR.
Sharp-eye Aggy was a raider and cultist of the Absolute who served at the Shattered Sanctum during the late 15 century DR.
Aeso was a junior Selûnite priest at Moonshadow Hall in Yhaunn during the late 14 century DR.
Adi was a female shu of the Jengi tribe who lived on the Malatran Plateau on the shores of the Lake of Giant Flies in the late 14 century DR.
Aglaera Rivenshaun was a traveling bard, highly-regarded in the nations of Chondath, Chessenta, and Turmish for her husky voice in the late 14 century DR.

Ahlmer was the shopkeeper of Ahlmer's General Store in the Port District of Procampur in the late 14 century DR. Ahlmer was formerly a thief. Although reformed, he was still in touch with the criminal underworld, such as it was in the law-abiding city.
Agga was a kobold from the Dragon's Rest cloister in the late 15 century DR.
Fist Aggralix was a member of the Flaming Fist who served the city of Baldur's Gate in late 15 century DR.
Agassaz was a Netherese arcanist who taught at the Inventor's Conservatory in Eileanar until its destruction in .
Afara was a Griefguard in the House of Grief temple that hid the Cloister of Sombre Embrace in the city of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Ada the Unbending was one of the retired adventurers inhabiting Nellie Thursday Home for Experienced Adventurers sometime in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Addington was a Netherese arcanist who taught at the Academy of Mentalist Study in Eileanar shortly before its destruction in .
Agnes Shveitz was the wife of Droona Shveitz of Baldur's Gate who was killed in the late 15 century DR.
Lord Adarl Summerstar was a noble of Cormyr in the late 15 century DR. He was the head of House Summerstar.
Adrielle was a devoted cleric of Helm and a member of the Anti-Hag Support Group of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Adreim was a carver living in Buckralam's Starn during the mid–8 century DR.

Adamor Thellik was a Constal of the Purple Dragons of Cormyr, who was stationed in the town of Eveningstar and commanded the defense of the town during the invasion from Sschindylryn in the late 15 century DR.
Adara Semple was a Morninglord of Amaunator that visited the Wheloon Prison in Cormyr in the late 15 century DR during the Shadovar invasion of Wheloon.
Adrik Ironcross was an illicit goods dealer at the Cutlass in Luskan during the late 15 century DR.

Adrian "the Twinblade" Carrathal was High King of Callidyrr from the mid–12 through the turn of the 13 century DR. Like his predecessors, although he held the title of High King of the Moonshae Isles, he was considered to be merely a figurehead by the Ffolk outside of Callidyrr.
Adom Kimball was a King of Moray in the Moonshae Isles during the early-to-mid 12 century DR.
Aghilde was a bog hag that lurked in the Druid's Deep of Thorngap during the late 15 century DR.
Agnar of Many Teeth was a great hunter and a merchant operating out of Port Nyanzaru in Chult during the late 15 century DR.
Agarta's belt was the personal belt of the brutal Night Brigade officer Agarta the Breaker in the late 15 century DR.
Battlemaster Agarta the Breaker was a senior officer of the Night Brigade gang in Wheloon Prison in the late 15 century DR.
Aeark was a human barbarian cleric terrorizing the countryside in the mid–14 century DR.

Agaza the Dreamweaver, who was known as the Witch o' the Woods among the inhabitants of the town of Lonelywood, was a night hag who settled in the Lonelywood Forest and operated under the guise of a druid of Mielikki in the late 14 century DR.
Aerwyll Sweetsong was an elven bard in the late 14 century DR.
Aelorin Ungive was a member of the Cormanthor Elves during the reclamation of Myth Drannor during the late 14 century DR.
Adarbron was a swordmaster captain of the guard in Hastarl during the early to mid-14 century DR.
Aghelyn was a Knight of Athalantar turned to banditry in the early 3 century DR.
Agathea was a powerful night hag who dwelled in the Underdark in the late 15 century DR.

Adamar Session was a bard, scholar, and teacher who lived in the city of Starmantle in the 14 century DR. Over a span of twelve years, he spent his youth as an adventurer, traveling across nearly the entirety of the Vilhon Reach. A year after retiring, at the age of 29, he authored a travel guide on the region.

Aeon was a goliath spymaster of unknown affiliation who operated out of the City of Splendors, Waterdeep, under the guise of a master tinkerer and a tavernkeep of the Greenhow tavern in the North Ward in the late 15 century DR.
Aglanna was a cultist of the Dead Three active in Baldur's Gate as of the turn of the 16 century DR.
Adair was a half-elf hunter in the Silent Slayers, a Shevarashi band of drow slayers, in the 14 century DR.

Adonis was one of a pair of house cats owned by the rogue Nimtu in the city of Ravens Bluff in the 14 century DR. Originally found in the wilderness alongside Venus, the two were kept around as pets and security on the Painted Boat.
Agorwal was a spokesman who represented Termalaine in the Ten Towns in Icewind Dale in the mid–14 century DR. Agorwal was a proud warrior and leader of the people of Termalaine.
Adrianna Wonceanyte was a resident of the city of Ravens Bluff in the mid-14 century DR.
Ahlimon was a sage living in Iriaebor in the Western Heartlands in the mid–14 century DR.
Aerilaya was a female green elf druid who came to live on Evermeet after wandering Faerûn for some time, spreading the faith of Rillifane Rallathil.
Aeramma Durothil was an elven sorcerer and a member of the Circle of Reilloch Domayr.
Ajantis Ilvastarr was a noble paladin of Helm and a knight of the Order of the Radiant Heart that lived during the mid–14 century DR.
Ahryn Firefinger was the leader of a dozen or so Red Wizards within their enclave in Mulmaster.
Lord Alaphondar Emmarask was one of the leading sages in service to the royalty of Cormyr in Suzail in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Alahar Khaumfros was the Waterbaron of Yartar during the mid–14 century DR. During this time, he was also the leader of the Kraken Society.
Akachi was a priest of the former god of the dead, Myrkul, who lived in Mulsantir in Rashemen.
Ajhuu was a powerful marid leader during the time of the Calim Empire.
Ak'hafta was a drow soldier hunting Drizzt Do'Urden in Mithral Hall for Vierna Do'Urden.
Aklar Delkash was a human man and merchant operating in the Vast in the late 1360s DR.
Lady Alauthshaee was an elf notorious for both her wealth and the manner of her death.
Albhaera Haerldoun was a Vaasan human woman. She was an adventurer and wizard, and owner of Haerldoun's Helms and Shields in the city of Wheloon in Cormyr.
Aileen was one of the Sisters of Synnoria, warriors of the Llewyrr.
Alarashan Tlor was a magelord of Athalantar during the first half of the 3 century DR.

Alansyn Ambrilar was a male human cleric of Lathander, the Morninglord, in Tantras in the Vast around 1358 DR. Ambrilar was High Morninglord of the Morning Halls temple to Lathander at the time. He led fourteen priests and twenty-one lay-followers.
Alaphale was a guard at the Agate Anchor curio shop in the city of Tantras in the Vast around 1358 DR.

Revered Father Akkabar el Souvlak was the head abbot of the House of St. Liwan's Blessing, an Ilmatari monastery on the western coast of Calimshan. Akkabar was a fat man who loved food and believed that his god, Ilmater, wanted to end the suffering of hunger. The abbey he ran was dedicated to preaching the appreciation of good food and diet.
Ailoth ( )) was an diviner and an agent of the Red Wizards of Thay for Sembia and Hillsfar. He was part of Alzegund's network.
Akyid al-Neti was the Headmaster of Al-Bidir Sallah, or the "Home of the Seekers of Knowledge", which was located in Huzuz, in 1367 DR.
Akura al-Hiyali was a member of the Corsair Council of Hawa and remained an active corsair captain despite his responsibilities in the city.
General Ahmahd abd al-Iffa directed the mamluks of the Honored Mamluk Society in Huzuz in 1367 DR.
Alatos "Ravenscar" Thuibuld was the leader of the thieves' guild known simply as the Guild in Baldur's Gate during the mid–14 century DR.
Akila Abd al-Amin was a caravan guard captain from Hiyal in Zakhara in 1367 DR.
Alak Faerzhind was the Master of Apportation of the school of Alteration in Sshamath in the year 1370 DR.

Ahlysaaria Yril'Lysaen was a female drow cleric of Lolth and a member of the mercantile House Lysaen of the city of Karsoluthiyl in 1370 DR. She was chosen to lead a group of three other priestesses and a 32-strong hunting party of her house to establish a hold on Level Two of Undermountain, with the goal of rebuilding an ancient slave-trading route to the surface, in order to bypass the route used by House Tanor'Thal, the ruling house of Karsoluthiyl.
Akir Abd al-Himaya was the commander of the Defenders Mamluk Society in Qudra in 1367 DR.
Al-Barq bin Mawli, or the Lightning, was a member of the House of Mawli in 1367 DR.
al-Asaf, or the Sorrowful, served as the cavalry of the efreet army in the City of Brass on the Elemental Plane of Fire.
Al-Warrakh, who was nicknamed the Charmer, was a bandit and member of the Desert Wind during the mid–14th century DR.
Aida al-Irrahman was a the true leader of the Winged Bulls in 1367 DR.
Akim al-Kalaas was a sha'ir and leader of the Unclean in 1367 DR. He had many nicknames, including the Sage, the Undaunted, Opener of Wisdom, and He Whom the Stars Obey.
Akima Abd al-Garib was a mamluk inhabiting the island of Afyal in east Zakhara in 1367 DR.
Akbara Abd al-Yahruq was a mamluk inhabiting Talab in Zakhara in 1367 DR.
Al-Bakbuk, or the Babbler, was a gibbering mouther living in the Pit of a Thousand Voices within Sarahin in 1367 DR.
Ainsbrith was a sage in Westgate and a member of the Guild of Naturalists. He was an expert on monster poisons.
Akkabar Shoon the Younger was the less-famous grandson of Akkabar Shoon the Elder, the mastermind behind the rise of the Shoon Imperium.
Ala'i ibn-Hasim was a dwarven sha'ir within the Palace of the Enlightened Throne in Huzuz, the City of Delights, in 1367 DR.
Akirakeiko was a sohei adventurer in Miyama Province in Kozakura in 1357 DR.
Akana Kiku was a wu jen adventurer in Kozakura in 1357 DR and 1358 DR.
Sherif Akyar al-Awasif was a noble djinni and a member of the royal court of Khedive Samia al-Sa'id of Rog'osto in east Zakhara in 1367 DR.
Albie Grizlow was a teenager cattle rancher in Uluvin, who lived there around the time of the War of the Silver Marches.
Alasz Ironwood was a sarcastic horse breeder and trader living in High Dale in the 14 century DR.
Alak Abaeir was a drow assassin under the employment of the church of Vhaeraun with membership in the same.
Alak Xorlarrin was a drow of House Xorlarrin and a twin son of the archmage of Q'Xorlarrin, Tsabrak Xorlarrin.
Alaecathra Shuinrond was the abbess of the Seekers of the Dawn in Myth Drannor in the Year of the Tankard, 1370 DR.

Alabhansree Alanasker, also known as Cymra Shanbadhe and "The Lady in Silver", was a Tashalan human and the former Chansreena (princess) of the city-state of Ormpur in Lapaliiya in southwest Faerûn in the mid–14 century DR.
Alastrah was a cloud giant who resided within Lyn Armaal during the late 15 century DR.

Alarim Renta was a half-orc leader of a human bandit gang that operated in the overland of Shadowdale in the year 1369 DR. His modus operandi was to intimidate passers-by to "donate" goods and gold for safe passage. His group was wary of increased patrols from Dagger Falls and fearful of Randal Morn and his Freedom Riders.

Aladiam was the proprietor of Aladiam's Imports, an imports shop found in Tegal's Mark during the mid-14 century DR. In addition to providing Sembian spices and silks from his store, he moonlighted as a smuggler and a fence, selling and transporting stolen goods. From his shop, he would often recruit adventurers and sell-swords to transport stolen goods for him.

Ai Ch'ing (), called the Mistress of Love and Fidelity, was one of the Nine Immortals who served the Celestial Emperor in the Celestial Empire, the dominant religion of Kara-Tur, particularly Shou Lung. She was the goddess of love, marriage, and fidelity and represented the virtues of love and fidelity in the Path of Enlightenment. As one of the Nine Immortals, Ai Ch'ing also held an important place in the Faith of the Nine Travelers.
Father Alby was a priest of Kelemvor who watched over the temple in Baldur's Gate during the late 15 century DR. He was assisted by a younger cleric, Nerys Kathon.
Ahmad ( ) was a gnome innkeeper inhabiting Dihliz in 1367 DR.
Ahmadora was a young girl living in Easthaven during the 11th century DR.

Alad bin Alaq bin Alonka was the Padishah of Medina al-Afyal in 1367 DR. Alad had a slew of titles and nicknames including His Most Enlightened and Resplendent Majesty, Servant of the Grand Caliph, Blood of Conquerers, Father of Multitudes, and Wise and Sage Master of His Own Destiny, but the one that stuck with him most was the Mad Padishah.
Alakbar bin Alad bin Alaq, or Alakbar for short, was the only male heir of the Padishah of Medina al-Afyal in 1367 DR.
Akbar bin Husam was a Zakharan sorcerer visiting Hiyal in Zakhara around 1367 DR.
Akmed was a tasked artist genie bound to an enchanted ring carried by Noora bint Amon in Zakhara around 1367 DR.

Akongo was one of the nyama-nummo, the offspring of the deity Olurobo in ancient Katashaka. Akongo was known by the ancient Tabaxi tribe to be a particularly perfidious entity dwelling in the southern highlands. When the couatl Ecatzin came to them to preach of Ubtao some time before , they were initially resistant, fearing the feathered serpent to be a minion of Akongo.
Akanna was a priestess of Cyrics who led her followers from within abandoned temple of Bhaal during the mid–14 century DR.
Alaffinel was a disgraced half-celestial of a noble line that fled his kin and was on the run circa 1370 DR along with his companion Methim.
Aki Marushima was a restaurateur who ran the well-known Aki's restaurant in the town of Aru in Wa in the 1770s on the Wa Calendar.
Ahrimanes was a demon lord titled the Chief of the Cacodaemons who presided over the 452 layer of the Abyss, Ahriman-abad. Ahrimanes was the patron of exiles and wanderers.
Ajan al-Yaqud was the leader of the members of House Bakr who chose to remain in the High Desert, as of 1367 DR, after their sheikh decided to live in Tajar.
Akamar al-Jawahirji was an accomplished merchant living in Huzuz, the City of Delights, around 1367 DR.
Alara bint Kira was a young noble of minor importance living in Huzuz, the City of Delights, around 1367 DR.
Alaghlar of the Horns was one of the archwizards of the Speculum, the Hall of Wizards of Myth Drannor long before the advent of the Weeping War.
Alassar Sulmander was a child servant at the keep at Caer-Dineval during the 1490s DR.
Ajloon was a shade who served the Night Guard of the Prince of Shade Yder Tanthul, for a brief period as his second-in-command, during the late 15 century DR.
Akrosz Ulvinhand was a human blacksmith who lived in the village of Amphail in the mid–14 century DR.
Alasitra was an abjurer and one of three minor wizards stationed at the enclave run by the young Red Wizard Hinnar.

Aikiko was a senator of Innarlith. She was among the senators allied with the clandestine Red Wizard Marek Rymüt. She was executed by Ransar Pristoleph in 1374 DR after the failed attempt by the senate faction to remove Pristoleph from power.
Ajaman was a warrior of the Qahtan tribe who roamed the deserts of Anauroch with his fellow tribesmen during the mid–14 century DR.
Al'Aif was a warrior Mtair Dhafir tribe during the mid–14 century DR.
Ahmad al-Rahib was a moralist and member of the League Conclave in I'tiraf in 1367 DR.
Aksonkor al-Daris was a moralist and member of the League Conclave in I'tiraf in 1367 DR.
Al'ia bint Hazir was the Chief Vizier of Gana in the Pearl Cities region of west Zakhara in 1367 DR.
Aisha al-Jazarijja was a member of the House of Hanif tribe within the Haunted Lands in 1367 DR.
Al Jilida was a ruthless, powerful schemer, and the local head of the slaver ring posing as the Sandvoyagers' Guild. He was in league with the guildhall at the Oasis of the White Palm.
Al-Dolak was the captain of the guard in Mobius Tower. He had been implicated in the ongoing assassination attempt on the tower.

Lady Regent Alasalynn Rowanmantle was a skilled warrior and Purple Dragon during the mid–14 century DR, and served as the ruler of the Cormyrean protectorate of Tilverton until the city's destruction in 1372 DR.
Ailon Finch was a cloth merchant in Ylraphon. He was slain by a black dragon in the Rage of Dragons of .
Most Exalted Fallskeeper Alatoasz Berendim was the high priest of Duskwood Dell in Amn.
Alayna was a hakima and the only daughter of Al'ia bint Hazir and Sultan Yusef al-Wadi of Gana in the Pearl Cities region of west Zakhara.
Alaodin was an assassin and follower of Bhaal. He ran an assassins' guild from Sentinelspire until he was supplanted by Chereth. He was also Talieth's father.
Aiden was an fallen aasimar from Norland isle on the Moonshaes who lived as a sailor and sea captain in the latter half of the 15 century DR.
Albryn Telnhand was a gnome leatherworker who lived in the Dock Ward of the city of Waterdeep in the 13 century DR.

Alberik was the captain of the guards at the path leading to Adama's Tooth, posted by the Datharathi to protect the access to their mine. In , he allowed Eined Datharathi into the mine despite being under standing orders not to let anyone in, as he had not been notified her family wanted her captured. Alongside her, he allowed in Ususi Manaallin and Iahn Qoyllor. The man had been a part to the indiscretions of the Datharathi heiress around the year , which made it more likely for him to take her statements at face value.
Akhenauben Bolphur was a famous crafter inhabiting Yeshpek along the Lake of Steam during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Alanaerle was the proprietor of the Weary Knight Inn in Arabel, Cormyr, in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Alataz Thrindol was a merchant from the city of Telflamm who once resided in the small town of Ravilar's Cloak in Turmish.
Alban Onire, the Holy Knight of Duty, was a legendary warrior loyal to Torm.
Alathan was a well-known martyred priest of Lathander who was active long before the 14 century DR.
Alair Nalabukhar was the fabled owner of an orb of power in the texts studied by Phelandern Ghemelt.
Alakin was the precept of the town of Aina in Mulhorand during the mid–14 century DR.
Akonhorus II was a the fifteenth pharaoh of Mulhorand during the mid–14 century DR.
Alavar was a harpist of some renown, active sometime before 1372 DR.
Ahri "Golemkin" was an artificer and an engineer from Lantan who worked in the illegal logging camp in Samarach by the Lantan-Samarach portal in the late 14 century DR.
Amath Sercent () was a priestess of Bane in Waterdeep during the early 1490s DR.
Ammalia Cassalanter () was a Waterdhavian noble in the late 15 century DR. She was the wife of Victoro Cassalanter.
Ambra Fallwater was a maid working in Baldur's Gate during the late 15 century DR. She was described as being rather plain-spoken.
Amrik Vanthampur () was the second youngest son of Thalamra Vanthampur of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
